## Done so far

I fixed `ranges/merge.py`:

**`merge_ranges`:** The original had two bugs — it never sorted the input (so unsorted ranges weren't merged correctly) and used strict `<` instead of `<=` (so touching ranges where `end == next start` weren't merged). It also mutated the input list in place. The fix sorts a copy of the input and merges with `start <= merged[-1][1]`, using `max` to keep the right end when one range contains another.

**`total_length`:** Was just summing `end - start` over all ranges (double-counting overlaps). Now delegates to `merge_ranges` and sums the lengths of the merged result, so overlaps are counted once.
